went_well: Your falling endings rose to 60%: in the stress drill, 7 of your 10 claims finished on a clear downward step.

mistakes.title: Questions disguised as statements
mistakes.evidence: 3 of the 10 claims ended with a rising pitch, all on sentences longer than 15 words.
mistakes.why: At a leadership briefing, a rise at the end of a claim invites challenge instead of agreement.
mistakes.try: Split long claims into two sentences and land the second one on a low, slow final word.

mistakes.title: Emphasis on the wrong word
mistakes.evidence: "Multi-turn attacks succeed where single prompts fail": the stress fell on "attacks", not on "multi-turn".
mistakes.why: The contrast is the point of the sentence; stressing it is what makes the claim memorable.
mistakes.try: Before reading, underline the one contrast word in each sentence and lean on it.

tomorrow: Statement endings: let the last word drop and slow down.
